h1: The 8 Best Robot Vacuums Under $500 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Robot Vacuums Under $500: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 robot vacuums under $500, scored on suction, mopping and docks, from roborock and Shark to eufy, Lefant and ILIFE.
summary: The roborock Q10 S5+ is the best robot vacuum under $500: 10,000Pa suction, a mop and a self-empty dock. The Shark AV2501S is the pet-hair pick with a bagless 30-day base, and the roborock Qrevo S5V adds the FlexiArm edge mop. The Q7 L5 is the budget combo, and the ILIFE V2 is the cheapest.
intro: Under $500 is the sweet spot for robot vacuums, and also where quality spreads the widest. At the top of the range you find self-emptying docks, LiDAR mapping and mop arms that extend to the baseboard. At the bottom you get a bare disc that bounces around the room and tangles on the first charger cable. The step between those two is larger than the price gap suggests.

We reviewed eight robots across that range and ranked them on what each step buys. Scores follow the Primea framework, with extra weight on dock convenience, mopping and how well each model fits a specific home, since floors and pets decide the right choice. Rankings come from spec sheets and owner reports.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: 10,000Pa, a mop and a self-empty dock. Everything people want in this bracket.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ pairs 10,000Pa suction with a vacuum and mop head, and it comes with a self-empty dock. That mix used to cost far more, and it defines the $200 to $500 bracket. Room mapping runs through the app. A dock matters because emptying a tiny bin every run is the chore that ends most owners' enthusiasm within a month.

It beats the Shark AV2501S because it adds a mop, and it beats the Qrevo S5V on price. The tradeoff is mopping: the Qrevo has a more capable mop system, so if wet floors matter most, look further down. Against the Q7 L5, the Q10 adds the dock and 2,000 more Pa.

Best for most households that want suction, mopping and a dock under one price ceiling. The caveat is that dock bags are an ongoing cost.
cons: Mopping simpler than the Qrevo S5V
Dock bags are an ongoing cost
products.idealFor: Most homes wanting suction, mop and dock in one.
products.skipIf: Mopping quality is your top priority.

products.name: Shark AV2501S AI Ultra Robot Vacuum with Self-Empty Base
products.verdict: A bagless HEPA base with 30 days of capacity. Built for homes that shed.
products.description:
The AV2501S sits on a self-empty base whose HEPA bagless bin is rated at 30 days. For a pet household that means fewer manual emptyings and no bags to buy, and the HEPA filter keeps fine dust contained. Shark's Matrix Clean navigation covers the floor in a grid pattern, and the robot builds a home map. It sells in the $200 to $500 range.

It does not mop, which is the one reason it sits behind the roborock. If your floors are mostly carpet and rugs, that matters little, and bagless operation can undercut the Q10's running cost. Against the Q7 L5, it adds a dock and filtration but no wet cleaning.

Pick it if you have dogs or cats and want to stop buying dock bags. The caveat is that the bin still needs emptying monthly. Skip it if you want a mop function.
products.idealFor: Pet households with carpet and rugs.

products.name: roborock Qrevo S5V Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: An extending FlexiArm mop reaches edges and corners. The most capable mopper here.
products.description:
The Qrevo S5V sits at the top of the bracket, with a FlexiArm that extends the mop pad toward walls and corners, something basic combos cannot do. LiDAR navigation maps more reliably than camera or bump systems, and the mop lifts automatically on carpet. It sells in the $200 to $500 range. Edge reach is the feature that justifies the premium.

It ranks third rather than first because it costs the most, and the Q10 S5+ does most of the same job for less. If you have lots of hard flooring with baseboards and cabinet bases to clean around, the extra reach is worth paying for. Against the Shark, it trades pet-friendly bagless design for mopping skill.

Choose it if sharp mopping along walls matters. The caveat is complexity: a carpet-heavy home gains little from the arm.
cons: More complex than needed for carpet homes
products.idealFor: Hard-floor homes with lots of edges to mop.

products.name: roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo
products.verdict: 8,000Pa and a mop at a budget price. Cheaper than the Q10 S5+ with the same core idea.
products.description:
The Q7 L5 delivers 8,000Pa suction and a mop attachment in the $100 to $200 range, well below the Q10 S5+. App control covers scheduling and basic zone selection, and it recharges and resumes on its own after a low battery stop. That auto-resume is what lets a small robot finish a larger floor in two passes.

What it loses against the Q10 S5+ is the self-empty dock and some of the more advanced zone controls. For a smaller home, you empty a dustbin occasionally, and the saving is worth it. Against the Tikom G8000 Max, it offers 3,000Pa more and a better-known brand.

Best for first-time buyers who want a mop combo from a proven brand without paying for a dock. The caveat is that hands-off emptying is not available. Skip it if you want a dock.
pros: Mop combo at a budget price
products.idealFor: First-time buyers of a mop combo.

products.name: Tikom Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo G8000 Max
products.verdict: 150-minute runtime with a physical remote. A budget combo for open hard-floor layouts.
products.description:
The G8000 Max is a vacuum and mop combo with a 150 minute maximum runtime, the longest among the budget combos, plus app and physical remote control. It sells in the $100 to $200 range. The remote is a useful fallback if you do not want to rely on a phone to start or steer the robot.

Suction is 5,000Pa, the lowest in the ranking, so it suits hard floors and light carpet rather than deep pile. The long runtime helps in a large open layout where a short battery would stop mid-job. Compared with the Q7 L5, it runs longer on paper but pulls less, and a lesser-known brand carries more support risk.

Good for open-plan hard-floor homes with light cleaning needs. The caveat is weak performance on thick carpet or heavy pet hair. Skip it for either.
products.idealFor: Open hard-floor homes with light cleaning needs.
products.skipIf: You have thick carpet or heavy pet hair.

products.name: eufy 11S MAX Robot Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: Thin, quiet and vacuum-only. It fits under low beds and cabinets that stop other robots.
products.description:
The 11S MAX skips mopping and app-based mapping. What that buys is a low profile that slips under furniture that stops boxier units, such as low beds and cabinet toe-kicks, and it runs quietly enough for daytime cleaning. It is vacuum only, with basic auto-charge, in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks sixth because it is basic next to the combos above, with no mop, no mapping and no dock. Against the Lefant M210, it costs more and offers less smart-home control, but it is the quieter, slimmer choice. Choose it for the fit and low noise, not the feature list.

Best for small homes with low furniture where clearance decides which robot works. The caveat is the missing mop and map. Skip it if you want mapping or mopping.
products.idealFor: Small homes with low beds and sofas.

products.name: Lefant Robot Vacuum Cleaner M210
products.verdict: 120 minutes of runtime plus app and Alexa control. Smart-home features for very little.
products.description:
The M210 only vacuums, runs for 120 minutes and takes Wi-Fi, app and Alexa commands, which gives it smart-home integration that undercuts many models near its price. It sells for $50 to $100. The slim profile helps with furniture clearance, and auto self-charging lets it return to base when the battery runs low.

Compared with the eufy 11S MAX, it adds app and voice control at a lower cost, though without that model's refinement. It does not mop and has no dock. Against the ILIFE V2 below, it offers longer runtime and app control for a similar price.

A good first robot for a small flat where basic daily vacuuming is enough. The caveat is a bare feature set with no dock or mapping. Skip it if you need a mop or a dock.
products.idealFor: Small flats and first-time robot buyers.
products.skipIf: You need a mop or a dock.

products.name: ILIFE V2 Robot Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: Tangle-free suction intake at the lowest cost here. A simple first or second robot.
products.description:
The V2 is the least expensive model in the guide, in the $50 to $100 range, and keeps things simple: an intake designed to limit hair wrapping the brush roll, automatic return to charge, and a compact bin. It has no mop and no room mapping. A tangle-free intake matters because hair wrapped around the roller is the most common reason a cheap robot stops.

It ranks last for that reason, but it also costs the least, so it works as a first robot or a spare for a small room. Against the Lefant M210, it gives up app and Alexa control. Against the eufy 11S MAX, it gives up the quiet, slim body.

Pick it for a small room or second floor where you only need hair and crumbs picked up. The caveat is a compact bin that fills fast. Skip it if you want mapping, mopping or a dock.
products.skipIf: You want mapping, mopping or a dock.

methodology.title: Feature per dollar
methodology.description: We compared what each robot gives you at its price step, from bare vacuums to docked mop combos.

methodology.title: Dock and upkeep
methodology.description: Self-empty docks, bagless bins and hand-emptied bins were ranked by how much work each leaves.

methodology.title: Mopping ability
methodology.description: Pad mops, auto-lift and extending arms were weighed against how well each should handle hard floors.

methodology.title: Navigation
methodology.description: LiDAR mapping, grid patterns and basic bumping were judged on how evenly each should cover a room.

methodology.title: Fit for the home
methodology.description: Height, noise and floor type were considered so each pick is matched to a specific kind of home.

whatMatters.detail: A self-empty dock moves dust into a larger bag or bin so you handle it every few weeks, not every run. It adds cost and size. If your home is small, a hand-emptied robot is fine. Check that the listing says dock included, since many cheaper listings sell the robot alone, and price bags into running cost.

Plain pad mops spread dirt on large floors, while auto-lift and extending arms handle carpet and edges. If your home has carpet, look for auto-lift in the spec bullets so rugs do not get wet. The Qrevo S5V lists auto-lift and FlexiArm, while the Tikom and Q7 L5 list only a mop function.

Pa numbers vary by brand and are rarely comparable across makers, and listing them at peak flatters every robot. Treat 8,000Pa and 10,000Pa as roughly the same tier, and spend more attention on brush design and filtration. A tangle-free intake matters more for long hair than a bigger pressure figure does. Check the brush type before you check Pa.

LiDAR or grid navigation plans rows and builds a map. Basic units bounce around and cover less reliably, and may miss corners. If you want room-based cleaning, read the listing for mapping, as on the Q10 S5+, Shark and Qrevo. The cheap vacuum-only units here mostly skip it, which is fine for one open room.

Measure the gap under your furniture. Slim robots fit under low beds, and quieter models suit daytime use. Compare the robot height with your gap before ordering, because a robot that does not fit simply will not clean there. The eufy 11S MAX is the slim pick, and the Lefant M210 also lists a slim profile.

faq.q: What can I get for under $500?
faq.a: A lot. The roborock Q10 S5+ and Shark AV2501S both include self-empty docks, and the Qrevo S5V adds an extending mop arm. Below that, budget robots like the Q7 L5 and ILIFE V2 cover basic vacuuming and some mopping.

faq.q: Is the Qrevo S5V worth more than the Q10 S5+?
faq.a: Only if you mop a lot of hard floor with edges. Its FlexiArm reaches corners. For most homes the Q10 S5+ gives similar everyday results for less, and adds the same dock, so the savings are real.

It helps in bigger homes, since it maps accurately and plans rows. In small flats, a basic robot like the Lefant M210 covers floors well enough, and LiDAR adds cost you may not need. Larger or multi-room homes get more from mapping.

faq.q: Will a cheap robot vacuum last?
faq.a: Longevity depends mostly on brush and filter care. Clean the brush roll weekly and replace filters on schedule. Cheaper units like the ILIFE V2 work well for light use if you keep the roller free of hair and empty the bin before it overfills.

faq.q: Are mop combos safe on carpet?
faq.a: Only with auto-lift or a carpet mode. The roborock Qrevo S5V lifts its mop automatically. Models without that feature, like the Tikom G8000 Max, should be kept off rugs using no-go zones in the app, or the pad will leave a wet stripe.
For hard floors and light carpet, yes, as with the Tikom G8000 Max. For deep pile or heavy pet hair, aim for 8,000Pa or higher, like the Q7 L5, and pair it with a self-empty dock.

finalTake: Buy the roborock Q10 S5+ for most homes. Choose the Shark AV2501S for pets and carpet, the Qrevo S5V for hard floors with long baseboards, and the Q7 L5 if you want a mop without a dock. The Tikom, eufy 11S MAX, Lefant and ILIFE suit small, simple homes. Decide on floor type and dock before price.
